FACT_ID: sec11-R01 | anchor: A01
Even where markings or signs allow passing, independently judge whether enough space makes the maneuver safe. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec11-R02 | anchor: A01
As a general practice, overtake one vehicle at a time rather than assuming room to pass several. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec11-R03 | anchor: A02
At 55 mph, the handbook estimates about ten seconds to pass, requiring corresponding oncoming-traffic and sight-distance gaps. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec11-R04 | anchor: A02
For passing near hills and curves, the source requires visibility of at least one-third mile, described as about ten seconds ahead. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec11-R05 | anchor: A02
When a curve or hill blocks the view, assume an approaching vehicle could be hidden beyond it. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec11-R06 | anchor: A02
Do not begin passing within one-third mile of a hill or curve. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec11-R07 | anchor: A02
Passing is hazardous at intersections, railroad crossings and shopping entrances where another road user may enter or cross. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec11-R08 | anchor: A02
The vehicle being overtaken can hide people, vehicles or trains from your view. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec11-R09 | anchor: A02
Drivers turning right into the lane you use to pass may not expect you there or check your direction. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec11-R10 | anchor: A02
Before overtaking, scan for conditions that may push other road users into your intended lane. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec11-R11 | anchor: A02
Pedestrians or cyclists near the roadway can reduce the space available for passing. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec11-R12 | anchor: A02
A narrow bridge, reduced lane width, ice, potholes or roadway debris can remove passing room. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec11-R13 | anchor: A02
Pass only when room exists to return to the driving lane; do not rely on others to create that room. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec11-R14 | anchor: A02
Do not overtake with a railroad grade crossing ahead. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec11-R15 | anchor: A02
Before returning after passing, leave enough clearance; the manual’s visual cue is seeing both headlights of the passed vehicle in the rearview mirror. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0028]
